textRuns.value: 1. Where: the Red River Delta is the hotspot. Viet Tri, Hung Yen, Hanoi, Bac Ninh and Nam Dinh average about 42-49 ug/m3 of Model PM2.5, roughly three times the WHO 24-hour guideline of 15. Only a few Cities average below it (Da Lat about 9; Buon Ma Thuot, Quy Nhon and Ca Mau about 12-13).

2. When: on page 1, the dry season (Nov-Apr) averages higher than the wet season (May-Oct) in every year shown, and March and April have the most city-days above the threshold. About two thirds of all city-days are above 15 ug/m3.

3. Weather: across Cities, neither temperature nor rainfall explains PM2.5 on its own. The highest Cities sit at moderate values (about 24-25 C, 5.5-6.5 mm/day) and warm or wet Cities range from about 12 to 27 ug/m3. These are 34 City averages, so this is a pattern to investigate, not a cause.

Recommendations: (a) focus air quality alerts and mitigation on the Red River Delta, especially from November to April; (b) do not forecast PM2.5 from temperature or rainfall alone; add wind, boundary layer height or emission data; (c) read these values as regional model estimates (CAMS, about 45 km, one City per Province), and confirm with station data before any policy use.
